_comment: Hand-maintained. Formats, limits and warning texts for the Decision API converter. Each format cites official pages (read 2026-11-19; the OpenAI pages re-read 2026-11-20). A null limit means the docs don't say: show 'limit not documented' instead of enforcing one. Fixtures: assets/js/tools/tests/fixtures/decisions/.

sources.quote: Send requests to `POST /v1/decisions` using `gpt-6-luna`, the only currently supported model.
Use an `input_json` content part to pass structured evidence without first converting it to a string. Put the JSON object or array in `data`.

sources.note: Score `levels`: 2 to 10, from the API reference (read 2026-11-19); no verbatim line stored.

sources.quote: Questions per request | 1 to 1,000 (bounded by the 262,144-token context window)
Before evaluation, the API sorts option keys alphabetically in UTF-8 byte order.
Conversation history, thought, and tool-call blocks aren't supported
Serialize JSON objects and arrays to a string

sources.note: Question keys match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`, up to 64 characters; choice `criteria` 2 to 255 options; score `criteria` 2 to 255 non-empty strings. From the Decisions API docs (read 2026-11-19); no verbatim line stored.

sources.quote: A System One request has `model`, `state` and `questions` (a map); score `criteria` has `maxItems: 10`.

sources.note: Choice `criteria`: 1 to 255 options, from the System One request schema (read 2026-11-19). The maximum question count isn't documented.

sources.quote: Clef follows the System One API, so you can switch an existing Jev integration to Clef by changing the endpoint and model. Ask up to 64 questions per request.

sources.note: Model page for `@cf/cloudflare/clef` (and `clef-flash`). Option limits and the `result` response wrapper are unconfirmed here.

criteria-folded.text: OpenAI predicates have no criteria field, so the yes/no definitions were appended to `instructions` as 'Yes means: … No means: …'. Re-check your threshold.

option-order.text: Gemini sorts option keys alphabetically, so your order isn't kept.
option-order.none_text: Alphabetical sorting places a `none…` option ahead of keys like 'shipping'.

score-merged.text: `label: description` merged into one string per level.

score-split.text: Each level string was split into `label` and `description`.

limit-exceeded.text: Over the target's limit. The request is still emitted so you can split it.

key-invalid.text: Key doesn't match the target's pattern, so it was sanitized.

unnamed.text: OpenAI question without `name`: generated a key.

json-stringified.text: JSON input wrapped as a string, because Gemini asks you to serialize JSON objects and arrays to a string.

history-serialized.text: Conversation serialized as `role: text` lines, because the target doesn't take conversation history.

media-manual.text: Media isn't converted; move it by hand.

box-unsupported.text: Jev `box` questions have no equivalent here, so it was dropped.

instructions-parts.text: Question instructions are text only on the target, so image or JSON parts were dropped.

probability-range.text: Yes/no probabilities always fall between 0.01 and 0.99. Set thresholds inside that range.

model-reset.text: Model set to the target's default; check that it's available to you.

endpoint-unverified.text: The Gemini REST path comes from third-party posts and SDK calls; check it in Google's API reference.

auth-unverified.text: We couldn't confirm Jev's auth header; check TypeSafe's docs.

migrate_flags.write-a-question: No description: we wrote a placeholder question. Rewrite it in your own words.
migrate_flags.describe-levels: Add a description to each level so the model knows what each score means.
migrate_flags.multi-label-split: Multi-label field: one yes/no question per value.
migrate_flags.use-answer-confidence: Decision APIs return probabilities and confidence for you, so this field was dropped.
migrate_flags.added-other: Nullable field: added an `other` option. OpenAI recommends a fallback option such as `"other"` when your categories don't cover every possible input.
migrate_flags.ordered-available: Ordered values? Turn on 'ordered' to ask a score question instead.

migrate_sources.quote: Use Structured Outputs… when you need to generate an object that follows your own JSON schema, such as extracted fields or a written explanation
Include a fallback option such as `"other"` when your categories don't cover every possible input

answers.openai: `{type: "score", name, score, probabilities: [{value, label, probability}], confidence}`
`{type: "refusal", name}` (`name` is `null` for an unnamed question)

answers.system_one: map keyed by question name (Clef wraps the response in `result`: unconfirmed)
